title: Sports Follow · Performance
description: How fast is it? API time taken (p50, p95, p99) overall, by fan journey and by route; from outside, by phase; moment to push; worker jobs' time and queue wait; the sources' time; the server's CPU, memory and load. deploy/RUNBOOK.md says what's normal.

panels.title: API p50
panels.description: Half of API requests over the range took longer than this (health checks and live streams aren't counted; the buckets make it approximate). From the API's side: a fan's phone adds the trip to Sydney.

panels.title: API p95
panels.description: The slowest 5% of API requests over the range took longer than this (health checks and live streams aren't counted; the buckets make it approximate). From the API's side: a fan's phone adds the trip to Sydney.

panels.title: API p99
panels.description: The slowest 1% of API requests over the range took longer than this (health checks and live streams aren't counted; the buckets make it approximate). From the API's side: a fan's phone adds the trip to Sydney.

panels.title: Outside p95
panels.description: The slowest 5% of the uptime checks from Mumbai and Singapore over the range, from DNS to the last byte of /api/health: what the trip to the server costs before any work.

panels.title: Push wait p95
panels.description: From a poll or build finding a moment (a goal, a wicket, a result) to its pushes going out, the slowest 5% over the range.

panels.title: Queue wait p95
panels.description: How long worker jobs waited for a slot before starting, the slowest 5% over the range. Long: polls, builds and pushes queue behind each other.

panels.title: Time taken by journey over the range
panels.description: Each fan journey's requests and how long they took (the runbook lists each journey's routes). A p95 over 1 s on a journey fans use often is worth a look; over 3 s for 10 minutes, "The API is slow" fires.

panels.title: Slowest routes over the range
panels.description: Every API route that answered in the range, slowest first by p95. A route with a handful of requests can top this on one slow one: read it with its count. A route whose few requests the metric hasn't timed (a process's first of each isn't) isn't listed; Health counts every request.

targets.expr: sum by (http_route) (label_replace(sum by (route) (count_over_time({service_name="sports-follow-api"} | scope_name="sports_follow.requests" | route != "/api/health" | route !~ ".*/stream" | route != "" [$__range])), "http_route", "$1", "route", "(.+)")) > 0

panels.title: From outside, by phase
panels.description: Each uptime check's time, by phase: resolve (DNS), connect (the trip to the server), tls, processing (Caddy and the API answering, plus one more trip), transfer. Connect and tls are the distance; processing is ours.

panels.title: API time taken, p50, p95 and p99
panels.description: Every API request together, each interval of the chart.

panels.title: Moment to push, p95
panels.description: From a moment found to its pushes, the slowest 5%, each interval of the chart. A gap: no pushes then.

panels.title: Job time taken p95, by job
panels.description: How long each worker (and curator) job ran, the slowest 5%. Lane jobs (engine_lane, poll_lane, history_lane) run for minutes by design; the top bucket is 15 minutes.

panels.title: Job queue wait p95, by job
panels.description: How long each job waited for a worker slot, the slowest 5%. "Jobs are waiting for the worker" fires when one has waited 2 minutes for 5.

panels.title: Source time taken p95, by host
panels.description: Requests to the data sources, the model gateway, push services and email, by host, the slowest 5%. The Sources dashboard has their errors and allowances.

panels.title: Server CPU
panels.description: Busy: the share of CPU time spent working. Held back: time Lightsail withheld (steal) once the burst allowance is used up; over 20% for 30 minutes alerts.

panels.title: Server memory free
panels.description: Memory available to the app's processes; under 5% for 10 minutes alerts. docker stats on the server says which container holds it.

panels.title: Server load
panels.description: Processes running or waiting for the CPU, averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes. Past the CPU count for long, work queues.
